votes.question: Booker Amdt. No. 6835 — To establish certain standards with respect to coaches of varsity sports teams.
votes.plain_language: This amendment would have let coaches move between four-year colleges under transfer rules like those for athletes, and it would have voided a coach's endorsement deal unless the pay matched similar non-coaches and had a real business purpose. A Yea would have added those rules. A Nay rejected them.

votes.question: Booker Amdt. No. 6805 — To increase the limitation on funding for post-eligibility insurance and catastrophic injury for student athletes.
votes.plain_language: This amendment would have capped a student-athlete insurance and catastrophic-injury fund at $200 million and required major conferences and an athletic association to cover any amount above $100 million. A Yea would have set that cap. A Nay rejected it.

votes.question: Kennedy Amdt. No. 6760 — To limit price increases for college athletics tickets.
votes.plain_language: This amendment would have barred colleges, conferences, and athletic associations from raising ticket prices for a sport by more than 4 percent from the prior academic year. A Yea would have added that cap. A Nay rejected it.

votes.question: Paul Amdt. No. 6758 — To improve the bill.
votes.plain_language: This amendment would have replaced the college-sports bill with the Collegiate Sports Integrity Act, which centers on an antitrust exemption for athletic conferences and associations. A Yea would have made that swap. A Nay rejected it.

votes.question: Baldwin Amdt. No. 6828 — To modify the provision relating to the relationship of this Act to existing law.
votes.plain_language: This amendment rewrites the college-sports bill's preemption section so states generally cannot set conflicting rules on athlete publicity pay, transfers, or certain eligibility, while keeping state civil-rights, contract, privacy, and similar laws unless they conflict. A Yea adopts that text. A Nay rejects it.

votes.question: H. Con. Res. 89 — A concurrent resolution directing the President, pursuant to section 5(c) of the War Powers Resolution, to remove United States Armed Forces from hostilities with Iran.
votes.plain_language: This House resolution tells the President to remove U.S. forces from hostilities with Iran unless Congress has declared war or authorized that force, while still allowing defense against an imminent attack. A Yea would agree to that direction. A Nay rejects the resolution.

votes.bill_title: Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026
votes.plain_language: This vote would end debate on whether to take up H.R. 7148 (Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026), which provides appropriations to several federal departments and agencies for the remainder of FY2026 and provides continuing FY2026 appropriations for the Department of Homeland Security through February 13, 2026. Cloture needs 60 votes (three-fifths of the Senate). A Yea moves the Senate toward taking up the bill; a Nay keeps debate open.

My Protect USPSTF Integrity Act would reestablish membership qualifications, requiring candidates are free of any conflicts of interest.

Tapping the Northeast Home Heating Oil Reserve may stabilize heating bills, but it does not erase the wider impacts of the administration's decisions.
https://t.co/Y3r93Ym8ju

So I am urging the Pentagon & @NOAA to ensure this data remains reliable & accurate

https://t.co/TzIEWYrxY7

Investing in Maine's future means keeping our state communities and industries connected to global markets – for a robust economy.
 
$37 million in federal funding will modernize railways in Aroostook County, improving safety and supporting local jobs.

Our backpedaling in Ukraine & missteps in Iran are harming our global alliances & security efforts around the world. https://t.co/0jxirMadRe

This Indigenous People’s Day is a day to honor the history, spirit, and minds of the people who authored the first chapters in Maine and America’s history. Not only did they lay the foundation for our nation, but their contributions should be heard and appreciated every day.

Deterrence has kept the US out of international conflicts for years, relying on the credibility & will of our military & relationship with allies
 
Yet our current posture is undermining this very credibility putting our nation’s safety & security at risk

https://t.co/gmVWtwYzf7

For 40 years, the Preventive Services Task Force has protected Americans' health through science-based data.

But after @HHSgov abruptly installed a new group with questionable qualifications, Americans are now at risk. My colleagues and I want answers.

https://t.co/Ntnn4DaQr9

We must make affordable housing easier to build, and support our American workers and manufacturers.
 
My bill would have @HUDgov recognize and share a vetted list of American-made products, streamlining the process for developers to follow federal rules.

https://t.co/2YsSR5moTc

The VA should provide the same coverage for veterans’ prescription drugs whether living on their own, in a nursing home or at a State Veterans Home.
 My bipartisan bill will allow veterans to receive the care they deserve, regardless of where they live
 
https://t.co/s0uHa4hdWE

The threat posed by AI isn't science fiction; it's fact -- and damn serious.
 
As these systems grow more powerful - and less predictable - I believe we have a responsibility to promote guardrails that ensure this technology strengthens our future.
 
https://t.co/H9ba6NrY5F

We celebrate National Lobster Day by honoring Maine's world class industry - a staple of our culture, and the backbone of our coastal economy.
 
Today we recognize the men and women in the fishery whose hard work brings 🦞from trap to table. https://t.co/PqlnWD00li

As cold weather approaches, heating oil prices are up 74 percent and threatening household budgets across Maine.
 
I’m calling on the President to release additional supplies from the Heating Oil Reserve – and lower the price we all pay out of pocket.
https://t.co/C0ne7P8xR8

Free and fair elections are the cornerstone of our democracy.
 
If the President is truly committed to protecting them, why has he fired so many government officials whose core mission is to keep our elections safe and secure?
https://t.co/MRcelV56Ld

Our veterans served our nation with distinction, and they deserve the best care after they’ve hung up their uniform.
 
My new bill would provide competitive salaries and maintain the strong standard of care provided at the VA.

https://t.co/0oFZFEH1GO

Today on #ConstitutionDay, we are motivated to move our nation toward a future that reflects our principles.
 The success of our experiment in self-government relies on understanding our shared past, national values, and the framers’ careful – though imperfect – vision.

Our students carry enough on their shoulders – not just the heavy textbooks, but academic stress and social pressures, too.
 
That's why I'm calling on the Department of Education to restore grant funding for school-based mental health services.

https://t.co/6oOYgaa5om

25 years ago today, our nation was attacked in the most horrific act of terrorism.
 
May we never forget the lives we lost—or the courage and unity Americans showed in the face of unimaginable tragedy. https://t.co/GQZOxJtW6d

In a normal administration, major decisions are made after a process involving gathering facts and data. It’s a variation on the old Reagan line — trust (your instinct) but verify (the facts).
 Unfortunately, this administration doesn’t work that way.https://t.co/A1pM7VYghZ

Mandating body-worn cameras, after spending $30.9 million, means little if ICE leaders only release footage they like.
 
Real transparency and accountability can’t depend on whether the video makes the agency look good. That defeats the entire purpose.
https://t.co/XpxW3c6iEK

Our servicemembers exposed to repeated blasts while protecting the U.S. deserve better protection for their health.
 
This new report shows we’ve made progress tracking blast-related brain injuries—but gaps still remain.
https://t.co/C1JzJbwmpn

One of the most historic speeches of the 20th century was given 63 years ago today.

I was fortunate to be there and hear Martin Luther King, Jr. share his dream. It was a day I’ll never forget & a powerful reminder that the work to build a more equal & just nation continues. https://t.co/C59KBP2cw6

Good news for Maine lobstermen: Canada removed American lobster from its retaliatory tariff list.

While this avoids a serious blow to Maine’s lobster industry, the broader trade war continues to create unnecessary uncertainty for Maine businesses and families. https://t.co/Pp9shcDMGA

Our National Parks belong to the American people.

Diverting nearly half a billion dollars from already-approved maintenance projects to pursue the White House’s pet projects is a disservice to our parks, their employees, and the millions who visit them.https://t.co/LjKrF42GUF

America’s national parks are “America’s Best Idea”—national treasures worth protecting and celebrating for generations to come.
 
This #NationalParkWeek is a reminder that these special places belong to all of us. Learn more ⬇️
https://t.co/0Piub3j3hQ

Every American agrees our servicemembers deserve safe living conditions & access to basic necessities.

The accounts from the USS Lincoln are deeply troubling. I’m demanding answers of the Pentagon to ensure the reported deplorable conditions are addressed.https://t.co/grUHXUvknJ

Maine people are proud of our trails, campgrounds, & lands; we also are vigilant about mosquitos & the diseases they carry.
 The SMASH Act would strengthen our nation's mosquito control efforts so Maine families ( & visitors) can enjoy the great outdoors.
https://t.co/mAo6dKqopK

financial_disclosures.caption: Official House financial disclosure filings from the Clerk of the House. A filing lists assets, income, liabilities, and trades the member reported; it is not proof of a conflict or of wrongdoing. Dollar ranges and asset names are in the PDF. This page links to the Clerk's copies and does not score anyone.
financial_disclosures.note: Senate financial disclosures are filed through efd.senate.gov, a different system from the House Clerk index used here. Senate filings are not listed yet.

funding.heading: Disclosed campaign receipts
funding.detail: Federal cards show the principal campaign committee and OpenFEC totals for one two-year cycle, plus itemized Schedule A contributors. House uses 2026. Senate uses the cycle of the next election (2026, 2028, or 2030). This is not career fundraising and does not include Schedule E outside spending. Governors do not get a federal contribution list.
